name: Monday Inbox
description: Triage a realistic inbox of 15 to 112 emails against a written rubric: a category from a fixed list for every message, and the owner, due date and priority (from exact rules, with a key-account exception) of every action. The inboxes contain lookalike-domain bank-details scams (one letter swapped), fake IT notices and gift-card "boss" emails, exact duplicates, meetings moved twice or cancelled, deadlines corrected (and corrected again), tasks reassigned twice, cancelled requests, chasers that repeat a request, forwarded emails whose quoted deadline is not a request, deadlines set "three working days before the site audit" when the audit later moves, a newsletter that tries to instruct the AI, and deadlines written as "next Wednesday", "within five working days" or "by the end of the month" across UK bank holidays. Every message is marked on its category and every action on its owner, due date and priority; an invented action costs as much as a missed one.
hook: A hundred emails, three scams, and a deadline tied to an audit that keeps moving. Can it clear your Monday?
author: Gauntlet Core
